dealAnnounced: 2000 (original partnership); November 17, 2015 (15-year extension and renaming to UPMC Rooney Sports Complex)

financials.source: UPMC Year End Financial and Operating Report, December 2025 (audited by Ernst & Young)

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: UPMC CY2025 Year End Financial Report — total cash and investments rose to $9.2B from $8.9B year-over-year
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Allegheny County tax-exempt property assessment records (2021); represents Allegheny County holdings only, statewide value is higher
balanceSheetWealth.notes: UPMC manages ~$10B in investment assets using an endowment-style approach with ~25% in alternatives (PE, VC, real estate, hedge funds, private credit, infrastructure). An additional $2.7B in cash and investments is held through regulated health and captive insurance companies. UPMC's internal investment office manages the portfolio.

bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: $1.6 billion — UPMC's largest issuance to date; $800M taxable fixed-rate, $571.3M tax-exempt fixed-rate, $250M direct purchase by JPMorgan Chase
bondDebt.source: UPMC CY2025 Year End Financial Report (bonds issued under 2007 Master Trust Indenture); Becker's Hospital Review; Bond Buyer

relatedOrganizations.source: Schedule R; Pennsylvania Insurance Department examination reports; UPMC CY2025 financial report ($17.6B insurance enrollment revenue); all ten insurance companies are 100% wholly-owned direct or indirect subsidiaries of UPMC

perks: Private jet usage reported by Pittsburgh City Paper
executiveComp.source: Form 990 FY2023 via Paddock Post and ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer; former CEO Jeffrey Romoff received $17,886,701 in deferred compensation payout in FY2023

communityBenefit.source: UPMC Annual Community Report FY2024 — nearly $2B total; $141M direct charity care/financial assistance; $605M unreimbursed Medicaid; UPMC cares for 18% of PA patients but claims 28% of hospital charity care statewide. Lown Institute ranked UPMC 5th worst nonprofit health system nationally with $601M fair-share deficit (FY2020 data). UPMC Presbyterian ranked least charitable nonprofit hospital in the nation by Lown.

taxAdvantage.notes: Property tax figure ($58.3M) is Allegheny County only (2021 data); UPMC owns $2.1B in tax-exempt property in that county alone. No PILOT agreement with Pittsburgh despite having PILOTs with four other PA municipalities (40-55% of full tax liability). City of Pittsburgh has repeatedly challenged UPMC's property tax exemption. Statewide foregone property tax is significantly higher.

layoffs.notes: Restructuring citing post-pandemic challenges; primarily non-clinical and administrative staff
200 workers laid off plus 300 vacant positions eliminated; non-clinical roles; criticized by labor representatives given $261M Q1 2026 profit
layoffs.source: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette; WPSU Radio; Healthcare Finance News

keyRiskFactors: Operating margin compression — swung from $211M operating loss in CY2024 to $286M income in CY2025
Insurance-provider integration risk via UPMC Health Plan ($506M insurance operating loss in CY2024)
Fitch outlook was negative before March 2026 revision to stable

acquisitions.notes: Merger created UPMC Pinnacle — expanded into central Pennsylvania

lobbying.source: OpenSecrets; PA state lobbying records show $740,000 in 2022 state-level spending; 2024 federal data not verified

legalIssues.description: City of Pittsburgh property tax exemption challenges — city has argued UPMC operates more like a for-profit business than a charitable nonprofit; UPMC owns $2.1B in tax-exempt property in Allegheny County with no PILOT agreement with Pittsburgh
legalIssues.status: Multiple rounds of litigation and settlement attempts

legalIssues.description: Consent decree with Highmark over network access for Highmark insurance members at UPMC facilities — state Attorney General involvement

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: UPMC holds 32x its annual operating income in investments, indicating massive accumulated wealth well beyond operational needs
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: UPMC carries $3.07 in tax-exempt bond debt for every $1 it claims in community benefit
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: State average not verified; Lown Institute ranked UPMC 5th worst nationally with a $601M fair-share deficit — spending less on charity care and community investment than the value of its tax exemption

accusation: Sits on $9.2B in investments, carries $6.1B in tax-exempt bond debt, reports a 0.85% operating margin on $33.6B in revenue, paid 25 executives $435M in a single year, and named the Steelers' training facility after itself.
